items.titleZh: 皮亚斯特里2026赛季正赛速度困境解析
items.summaryZh: 皮亚斯特里在2026赛季与诺里斯的正赛速度差距明显，奥斯汀站同策略下平均每圈慢半秒、最终落后22秒，他坦言目前还无法解释原因。
items.originalTitle: 'Superpower' neutered - Piastri’s fresh F1 struggles explained
items.summaryEn: Oscar Piastri is facing a clear race-pace deficit to Lando Norris in the 2026 season, averaging half a second per lap slower on the same strategy in Austin and finishing 22 seconds behind, and he admits he cannot yet explain why.
detailZh: 奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里在2026赛季的迈凯伦赛车上正经历与队友兰多·诺里斯相比的新困难，其中包括一个让车队领队安德烈亚·斯特拉所称的他的“超能力”失效的周末。
排位赛中诺里斯占据上风，以16比8领先皮亚斯特里，但两人之间的实际平均差距仅为0.040秒。
更明显的差距出现在不少大奖赛中，包括奥斯汀站。同策略下，皮亚斯特里（绿线）在正赛中平均每圈比诺里斯（橙线）慢半秒，最终落后22秒。此前还有巴塞罗那站（落后35秒）和赞德沃特站（落后32秒）这样差距巨大的周末，他承认“现在有太多比赛差距真的很大”。
被问及正赛速度的问题所在时，皮亚斯特里回答：“很慢。目前我没有更多可说的。”
“当伊萨克·哈贾尔从维修区出来时，看起来他遇到了某种问题，他的能量部署有点混乱。所以我在一些尴尬的位置追近了他，在那里损失了不少时间。
“从那之后，我在比赛剩余时间里基本上都在防守乔治·拉塞尔。但我觉得除此之外，速度显然不够好。所以有很多东西需要去弄明白。”
这对皮亚斯特里来说是一个挣扎的周末，因为虽然纸面上他在排位赛中击败了诺里斯——而且皮亚斯特里确实值得一些肯定，因为他做出了一个更快的合法圈——但他实际上比诺里斯最快的（因超出赛道限制被删除的）第三节排位赛圈速慢了0.424秒。
到周六时，皮亚斯特里的速度劣势已经非常明显，以至于迈凯伦在赛前会议上已经考虑到了可能需要交换两辆车的顺序，因为——正如车队领队斯特拉所说——“我们在周末期间看到兰多比奥斯卡稍快一些”。
皮亚斯特里在周五称奥斯汀站“从第一圈起就很艰难”，并补充道：“仅仅想让赛车发挥出性能就已经非常、非常具有挑战性了。”
“在排位赛的某些阶段，至少对兰多来说，赛车看起来是有潜力的，我觉得我们俩都感觉它确实有潜力。但能否把这份潜力挖掘出来，差距大概有半秒之多。”
“要从这辆赛车里榨出那个圈速真的非常、非常困难。我完全没能做到，但我觉得当我们俩中任何一人真正去推到极限时，就没法把车留在赛道上了。这确实是非常具有挑战性的一站。”
2026年的迈凯伦赛车确实具有刀锋般的特性，但诺里斯今年无疑更好地应对了这些。
最明显的对比是迈凯伦在夏休期前后的强势表现，如果没有马德里那次时机不佳的虚拟安全车，诺里斯本可以赢下四场比赛中的三场，而皮亚斯特里甚至没有登上领奖台（自五月初迈阿密以来也再未登台）。布达佩斯是皮亚斯特里最好的机会——在套圈卡洛斯·塞恩斯时的不幸接触让他错失了机会——但即便在那里，他在速度上也明显落后诺里斯一步。
但皮亚斯特里和迈凯伦认为他在最近几轮取得了进步，迈凯伦F1首席执行官扎克·布朗在新加坡表示，他“喜欢我在奥斯卡身上看到的一切，他感觉自信多了，完全掌控局面”。
皮亚斯特里相信自己已经解决了赛季初的一些弱点——但新的问题正在出现，这意味着结果看起来是一样的。
“这远没有我想要的那么有竞争力，”皮亚斯特里在奥斯汀说。
在我原本以为会很挣扎的弯道，以及今年一直很吃力的那类弯道，这个周末其实相当不错，但更多只是关于如何把整圈的所有环节拼在一起。
这才是真正的挑战。我不觉得情况与赛季早些时候完全相同，但最终结果仍然一样。
有点遗憾，但我对此并不太失望，因为我觉得自己一直在努力的方面仍然在展现出进步。
“超能力”被废掉了？
皮亚斯特里去年在奥斯汀也确实表现挣扎，最终获得第五名，而诺里斯则领先超过20秒获得第二名。
因此，这条赛道对皮亚斯特里来说相对不利，正如斯特拉在赛后所指出的那样。
“这是一条兰多擅长的赛道，也是奥斯卡相对更挣扎的赛道之一，”斯特拉说道。
“所以今年，我认为对奥斯卡来说尤其棘手，因为奥斯卡的超能力是逐步建立。一旦他建立起参照点，他就能真正高效地一圈接一圈地推进。但在这里，每一圈都不同。所以这些条件对奥斯卡构成了挑战。
“实际上，这些正是兰多发挥自己超能力的条件，那就是对条件极具适应性，尤其是在赛车打滑的时候。”
正是这种困难，皮亚斯特里整个赛季都在努力克服。他在2025年初展现出的状态，今年对他来说几乎完全遥不可及。在奥斯汀，这是因为不断变化的条件，而在此之前，则是试图重复那种与2026款动力单元契合良好的驾驶输入。
“这辆车需要付出相当大的努力才能做出圈速，并且需要驾驶输入达到比去年高得多的强度，”斯特拉在新加坡解释道——当时人们还希望皮亚斯特里在2026年的挣扎已经过去。
“这是车手们花了一些时间才适应[的]——好吧，‘适应’这个词不对，应该是理解。这也是奥斯卡在某个阶段几乎失去与兰多相比的部分竞争力的原因之一。
奥斯卡只需要明白如何迫使赛车做出一些事情，并接受开得快不一定意味着开得干净。
相反，这大概是奥斯卡的标志性特点，过去我们看到他快的时候，他开得很干净，那是非常好的数据，非常可重复，而且他很快。
“用这辆车，所有这些事情加在一起，似乎并不经常同时发生，所以对车手来说工作量很大。”
皮亚斯特里不得不适应，因为迈凯伦带来的升级都没有让赛车的最佳工作窗口变得更宽。
皮亚斯特里表示：“这些升级实际上都没有让赛车更容易驾驶，而这正是我们最大的问题。”
因此，本赛季这辆赛车不会变得适合皮亚斯特里，而且也不能保证迈凯伦能在2027年为赛车消除这种刀锋般的敏感特性。
车队希望拓宽性能窗口，让两位车手都能更容易地发挥出圈速，但归根结底，迈凯伦的首要任务是打造一辆快车。
而皮亚斯特里很可能要度过一个漫长的冬天，努力寻找答案，弄清楚如何在这些新规则下持续重新追平诺里斯。
detailEn: Oscar Piastri is experiencing new difficulties with the 2026 McLaren compared to team-mate Lando Norris, including a weekend that neutered what team boss Andrea Stella calls his ‘superpower’.
In qualifying, Norris has had the upper hand as he leads Piastri 16-8, but the actual average gap between them has only been 0.040s.

The more stark gap has been in a good number of grands prix, including Austin. Piastri (green line) is on average half a second slower than Norris (orange line), through the race on the same strategy, and ends up 22 seconds behind. This follows other weekends with big deficits like Barcelona (35 seconds) and Zandvoort (32 seconds), where he admitted there were “too many [races] now that have been really a long way off”.
Asked what the issue with his race pace was, Piastri replied: "It was slow. I don't have any more than that at the moment.

“When [Isack] Hadjar came out of the pits, it looked like he had some kind of issue and his deployment was a bit all over the place. So I was kind of catching him in awkward places and lost a fair bit of time there.
“Then I was kind of defending from George [Russell] for the rest of the race from that. But I think on top of that the pace just clearly wasn't very good. So plenty to try and understand.”

It was a weekend-long struggle for Piastri, as while on paper he outqualified Norris - and Piastri does deserve some credit for setting a faster legal lap - he was actually 0.424s behind Norris’s fastest (track limits-deleted) Q3 lap.

Piastri’s pace deficit was so clear by Saturday that McLaren had factored in the potential need to swap the cars' order in their pre-race meetings, because - as per team boss Stella - "we had seen during the weekend that Lando was a little bit faster than Oscar”.
Piastri called Austin “tough from lap one” on Friday, adding, "Just trying to get performance out of the car has been very, very challenging.

“At points in qualifying, for Lando at least, it looked like there was potential in it and I think we both felt there is potential in it. But the difference of extracting that potential or not is like half a second different.

"It's been very, very tough to get that laptime out of the car. I've not managed it at all, but I think when either of us have really pushed the boundaries, we can't keep it on the track. It's been a very challenging one, for sure.”
The 2026 McLaren does have knife-edge qualities, but Norris has undoubtedly dealt with those better this year.

The clearest contrast was McLaren’s purple patch either side of the summer break, where Norris would have won three out of four races without a poorly timed virtual safety car in Madrid, while Piastri didn’t even feature on the podium (and hasn’t since Miami in early May). Budapest was Piastri’s best chance - unfortunate contact while lapping Carlos Sainz robbed him of it - but even there, he was a clear step behind Norris on pace.

But Piastri and McLaren feel he’s made progress in recent rounds, with McLaren F1 CEO Zak Brown saying in Singapore that he was “liking everything I see out of Oscar, he's feeling much more confident, on top of things”.
Piastri believes he has fixed some of his weaknesses from earlier in the season - but new ones are appearing, meaning the outcome looks the same.
“It’s not been anywhere near as competitive as what I wanted it to be,” Piastri said in Austin.

“In the corners that I thought would be a struggle and the types of corners that have been a struggle this year, it's been pretty good this weekend, but it's more just been about trying to get everything in the lap together.
"That's been the real challenge. I don't think it's quite the same picture as what it has been earlier in the season, but the end result is still the same.
“It's a bit of a shame, but I'm not too disappointed in that because I feel like the areas I've been working on are still showing progress.”
'Superpower' neutered?
Piastri did also struggle at Austin last year, finishing fifth while Norris was over 20 seconds up the road in second.
So there is an element of this being a less favourable track for Piastri, as Stella pointed out after the race.
"This is a track in which Lando excels, and is one of the tracks in which Oscar instead struggles a little bit more,” Stella said.

"So this year, I think in particular for Oscar, it's tricky because Oscar's superpower is to build. Once he creates references, he can really effectively build lap after lap. But here, every lap is different. So these are the conditions that challenge Oscar.
“Actually, [these] are the conditions where Lando uses his own superpower, which is being very adaptive to the conditions, especially as the car slides.”

It’s that difficulty that Piastri has been fighting to overcome all season. His early-2025 form has looked almost completely inaccessible to him this year. At Austin it was because of the changing conditions, whereas previously it’s been trying to repeat the kind of driving inputs that mesh well with the 2026 power units.

“The car needs quite a lot of effort to deliver laptime and it requires a level of intensity in the driving input which is much superior to last year,” Stella explained in Singapore - when there were hopes Piastri’s 2026 struggles were behind him.

"This is something that took some time for the drivers to get comfortable [with] - well, 'comfortable' is wrong, but to understand. And it's also one of the reasons why Oscar, at some stage, he almost lost some of the competitiveness compared to Lando.
"Oscar just needed to understand how to force the car to do some things and [accept] the fact that driving fast will not necessarily mean driving clean.
“Instead, probably the signature of Oscar, when we have seen him fast in the past, [is] he was clean, it was really good data to see, it was very repeatable and he was fast.
"With this car, all these things together, they don't seem to happen very often, so it's a lot of work for the drivers.”
Piastri’s had to adapt because none of the upgrades McLaren has brought has made the car’s optimal operating window any wider.
“None of these upgrades are really making the car easier to drive, which is kind of our biggest problem,” Piastri said.
So the car isn’t going to come to Piastri this season, and there’s no guarantee that McLaren will be able to eliminate this knife-edge trait from its car for 2027.
The team wants to open up the window of performance so the laptime can be more easily accessed by both drivers, but ultimately McLaren’s number one priority is making a fast car.
And Piastri is likely to have a long winter trying to find the answer to how to consistently get back on terms with Norris in these new regulations.

items.titleZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳承认在获得6700万英镑的赔偿后无需回归F1
items.summaryZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳离开红牛车队后，由于获得了巨额赔偿金，他无需在赛道上寻找新角色。

items.originalTitle: Christian Horner admits he doesn't need F1 return after £67 million Red Bull payout
detailZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳承认，在获得6700万英镑的雷诺车队赔偿后，他不需要回到F1
克里斯蒂安·霍纳在一次揭露性的新采访中谈到了他在F1的未来以及他的6700万英镑的离职赔偿金
对于红牛车队的粉丝来说，关注红牛车队，了解F1新闻、车手更新、技术洞察和米尔顿凯恩斯的比赛分析
当一位高调的F1高管被解雇时，谣言机器立即转向他们下一个可能落脚的地方。但就克里斯蒂安·霍纳而言，他在2025年离开红牛车队时，得到了如此巨大的金降落伞，以至于完全改写了他的职业轨迹。
而不是急于在维修区争取一个新的角色，这位52岁的老将正在为自己的F1生涯结束后作为一位高度流动的自由球员的生活进行规划。在最近的一次澳大利亚60分钟的节目中，焦点从导致他下台的职场政治转向了对可能回归的经济分析。由于提前终止合同，他的银行账户得到了大幅增强，霍纳正从绝对有利的位置计算着他的下一步行动。
当红牛GmbH终止了他的雇佣关系时，霍纳的合同还有四年多。解约的财务损失最近被揭露。根据红牛技术有限公司2025年的财务报告，霍纳获得了一笔惊人的6700万英镑（约合8850万美元）的赔偿金，一些车队的消息人士估计，一旦解决了额外的合同费用，总金额可能接近1亿美元。
这样的财富水平从根本上改变了霍纳对下一步职业发展的看法。
霍纳在直播中解释说：“我认为这给了我时间上的奢侈，我处于一个不需要回到一级方程式的有利位置。我认为生活中最宝贵的东西就是时间。”
尽管霍纳在英格兰乡村庄园享受着宁静的生活，并且目前正为英国美洲杯帆船队提供咨询，但他迅速确认自己的竞技动力并未消退。
“我仍然是个速度狂热者，”霍纳承认。“所以无论是四轮、两轮、四条腿……用马。给我看看赛道。”
车库里普遍认为，霍纳作为传统、拿薪水的雇员的日子已经结束。在直播中，记者塔拉·布朗指出，尽管关于他回归一级方程式的传言仍在流传，但霍纳只有在“他拥有车队的一部分所有权”的情况下才会回来。
在红牛的20年统治期间，霍纳是车队成功的终极建筑师，但他从未拥有过运营的股份。现在，霍纳拥有九位数净财富，这种动态已经完全改变。
如果一个陷入困境的中场车队或即将到来的制造商想要利用霍纳的冠军级专业知识来重建其项目，它必须提供董事会席位，而不仅仅是维修区。购买车队的一小部分股份立刻将霍纳从一名可替换的员工提升为特许经营伙伴。
无论他决定花钱重返赛道，还是选择退休专注于自己的赛马，这位前红牛智囊已经确保任何未来的谈判都将完全按照他自己的条款进行。
detailEn: Christian Horner admits he doesn't need F1 return after £67 million Red Bull payout
Christian Horner addresses his future in Formula 1 and his £67million severance package in a revealing new interview
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

When a high-profile Formula 1 executive is shown the door, the rumour mill immediately shifts to where they will land next. But in the case of Christian Horner, his departure from Red Bull Racing in 2025 came with a golden parachute so immense that it completely rewrote his career trajectory.

Rather than scrambling to secure a new role on the pitwall, the 52-year-old is navigating his post-F1 reality as a highly liquid free agent. During a recent feature on 60 Minutes Australia, the focus pivoted away from the corporate politics that caused his downfall and honed in on the pure economics of a potential comeback. With a bank account heavily reinforced by an early contract termination, Horner is calculating his next move from a position of absolute leverage.

When Red Bull GmbH terminated his employment, Horner still had over four years remaining on his contract. The financial toll of severing that agreement was recently laid bare. According to Red Bull Technology Limited's 2025 financial reports, Horner received a staggering payout of £67million (approximately $88.5million), with some paddock sources estimating the total package closer to $100million once additional contractual fees were settled.
That level of generational wealth has fundamentally shifted how Horner approaches his next career move.

"I think it gives you the luxury of time, that I'm in a privileged position that I don't need to go back to Formula 1," Horner explained during the broadcast. "The most precious thing I think in life is time."

Despite embracing a quieter life on his English country estate and currently consulting for the British America's Cup sailing team, Horner was quick to confirm that his competitive drive has not faded.
"I'm still a speed junkie," Horner admitted. "So whether it's on four wheels, two wheels, four legs... with horses. Show me the racing line."

The consensus within the paddock is that Horner’s days of being a traditional, salaried employee are over. During the broadcast, reporter Tara Brown noted that while rumours of a Formula 1 return continue to swirl, Horner will only come back "if he has some ownership of a team".

Throughout his 20-year reign at Red Bull, Horner was the ultimate architect of the team's success, yet he never possessed an equity stake in the operation. Now that Horner is armed with a nine-figure net worth, the dynamic has completely changed.

If a struggling midfield constructor or an incoming manufacturer wants to leverage Horner's championship-winning expertise to rebuild its programme, it will have to offer a seat at the boardroom table, not just the pitwall. Purchasing a minority stake in a team instantly elevates Horner from a disposable employee to a franchise partner.

Whether he decides to buy his way back onto the grid or stays in retirement focusing on his racehorses, the former Red Bull mastermind has ensured that any future negotiations will be conducted entirely on his own terms.

items.originalTitle: Mark Webber's Red Bull exit branded "disrespectful" as Daniel Ricciardo praised
detailZh: 马克·韦伯的红牛离职被批不尊重，丹尼尔·里卡多获赞誉
克里斯蒂安·霍纳回顾了马克·韦伯2013年的不尊重离职，并赞扬了丹尼尔·里卡多的红牛车队巅峰时期
丹尼尔·里卡多、克里斯蒂安·霍纳、红牛车队
对于红牛车队的粉丝来说，关注红牛车队，了解F1新闻、车手更新、技术洞察和赛事分析
红牛车队与澳大利亚车手有着漫长且高度复杂的历史。马克·韦伯在塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔夺冠的年份帮助车队建立了胜利的基础，而丹尼尔·里卡多接过接力棒，在涡轮增压混合动力时代的黎明时期领导了车队。
在最近的一次60分钟澳大利亚访谈中，克里斯蒂安·霍纳回顾了这两位男士在他的团队中的运作方式。摆脱了标准的公关套话，霍纳在比较韦伯任期结束的苦涩与里卡多爆炸性到来的时刻时毫不保留。
到2013年，马克·韦伯与红牛的关系已经彻底破裂。马来西亚大奖赛上的臭名昭著的"多21"事件将韦伯和塞巴斯蒂安·维特尔的激烈竞争推向了临界点。
在2013年英国大奖赛前的星期四，韦伯宣布了他将在赛季结束时退役。但这位澳大利亚车手选择直接向媒体发布他转投保时捷的消息，而没有先面对面通知霍纳。十多年后，这种退出策略的刺痛感仍然是前车队老板难以忘怀的记忆。
马克·韦伯，克里斯蒂安·霍纳，红牛车队负责人
“当他以那样的方式离开时，我只是感到很悲伤，”霍纳直言不讳地说。“我认为这对车队也很不尊重。”
霍纳指出，随着时间的推移，他有了新的看法，两人现在关系良好，但宣布离职时向媒体而不是车队负责人通报，这种公司层面的轻视显然留下了深刻的印象。
韦伯的离开为丹尼尔·里卡多打开了大门，他在2014年晋升到红牛车队。虽然来自青训车队托罗罗索，但红牛管理层内部确实对他的精英赛车技巧是否足以在发车线上竞争表示怀疑。
霍纳解释了当里卡多被安置在赛车中后，那些疑虑是如何迅速消除的。
“我们的犹豫是因为我们没有看到他超越太多车辆，然后当他开上红牛赛车时，他从未停止超越别人，”霍纳回忆道。 “他成为了刹车上的动物，并在我们这里的第一年赢得了三个大奖赛。”
丹尼尔·里卡多，红牛车队，克里斯蒂安·霍纳，车队负责人，红牛车队
这三次胜利发生在加拿大大奖赛，还有匈牙利和比利时的胜利。在梅赛德斯车队完全主宰赛季的情况下取得这样的成功——并且在同一车库中常规性地超越四届卫冕冠军维特尔——巩固了里卡多在现代一级方程式历史上顶尖后刹车手之一的地位。
霍纳的反思突出了红牛车队所需的激烈、高风险的车手管理，展示了如何迅速将一名未经证实的候选人变成车队传奇，以及一名老将的离开如何轻易变得糟糕。
detailEn: Mark Webber's Red Bull exit branded "disrespectful" as Daniel Ricciardo praised
Christian Horner reflects on Mark Webber's "disrespectful" 2013 exit and praises Daniel Ricciardo's prime Red Bull era
Daniel Ricciardo, Christian Horner, Red Bull Racing
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

Red Bull Racing has a long, highly complicated history with Australian drivers. Mark Webber helped build the team's winning foundation during Sebastian Vettel's championship years, while Daniel Ricciardo took the baton and led the garage at the dawn of the turbo-hybrid era.

In a recent 60 Minutes Australia interview, Christian Horner offered a look back at how both men operated within his team. Free from the standard corporate PR lines, Horner did not hold back when comparing the bitter end of Webber's tenure to the explosive arrival of Ricciardo.

By 2013, the relationship between Mark Webber and Red Bull was thoroughly fractured. The infamous "Multi 21" saga at the Malaysian Grand Prix had pushed the intense rivalry between Webber and Sebastian Vettel to a breaking point.

On the Thursday before the 2013 British Grand Prix, Webber announced his retirement from Formula 1 for the end of the season. But the Australian driver chose to release the news directly to the media regarding his move to Porsche without informing Horner face-to-face first. Over a decade later, the sting of that exit strategy remains a defining memory for the former team boss.
Mark Webber, Christian Horner, Red Bull team principal
"I was just sad when he left that he did it in the manner that he did," Horner stated bluntly. "I thought it was disrespectful to the team as well."

While Horner noted that the passage of time has provided perspective and that the two men are on fine terms today, the corporate slight of announcing a departure to the press rather than the team principal clearly left a lasting impression.

Webber's departure opened the door for Daniel Ricciardo, who was promoted to Red Bull in 2014. Coming from the junior Toro Rosso squad, there were genuine doubts within Red Bull management about whether Ricciardo had the elite racecraft necessary to battle at the front of the grid.
Horner explained how quickly those doubts were erased once Ricciardo was put in race-winning machinery.

"Our hesitation was that we hadn't seen him overtake too many cars, and then when he got in the Red Bull car he never stopped overtaking people," Horner recalled. "He became an animal on the brakes and won three Grand Prix in his first year with us."
Daniel Ricciardo, Red Bull Racing, Christian Horner, Team Principal, Red Bull Racing

Those three victories came at the Canadian Grand Prix, with further wins in Hungary and Belgium. Achieving that success during a season utterly dominated by the Mercedes team - and routinely outperforming the four-time defending champion Vettel in the same garage - firmly established Ricciardo as one of the premier late-brakers in modern F1 history.

Horner's reflections highlight the intense, high-stakes driver management required at Red Bull, showcasing how quickly an unproven prospect can become a team legend, and how easily a veteran's exit can turn sour.

items.originalTitle: Christian Horner reveals why Netflix made him the villain of "Drive to Survive"
items.summaryEn: Christian Horner addressed how Netflix's "Drive to Survive" edited him into a villain and discussed how the show transformed his public image in Formula 1.
detailZh: 克里斯蒂安·霍纳揭示Netflix为何让他在《极速求生》中成为反派
克里斯蒂安·霍纳回应了他在《极速求生》中引发两极评价的反派剪辑，以及Netflix如何改变了他的F1声誉
致红牛车迷。关注红牛车队，获取来自米尔顿凯恩斯的F1新闻、车手动态、技术洞察与比赛分析。
在Netflix把摄像机带进F1围场之前，车队领队大多被视为在维修区墙边冷静指挥、精于算计的管理者。到克里斯蒂安·霍纳离开时，这一角色已演变为完全不同的形态。他不再只是一名赛车高管，而是全球电视上最具辨识度、也最受激烈争议的反派人物之一。
霍纳在接受澳大利亚《60分钟》节目采访时，谈到了彻底改变他公众声誉的巨大文化转变。尽管一些前围场人物对他们在《极速求生》中的形象深感不满，但这位52岁的领队对自己那臭名昭著的“反派”剪辑持非常务实的态度。
在播出多季的过程中，这部Netflix纪录片系列大获成功，它把一级方程式赛车不仅呈现为一项赛车运动，更呈现为一场高风险的 corporate 肥皂剧。
这场闹剧的中心人物是霍纳，他经常与梅赛德斯领队托托·沃尔夫和迈凯伦首席执行官扎克·布朗针锋相对。制作团队利用了每一次新闻发布会上的讽刺言论、每一次摔耳机的动作，以及每一场激烈的政治争端——从2021年阿布扎比那场爆炸性的总冠军决胜战，到红牛2022年广为人知的预算帽违规事件。
克里斯蒂安·霍纳，红牛车队领队
霍纳对于制作团队如何剪辑那些互动以打造出引人入胜、高度戏剧化的叙事，并不抱任何幻想。
“他们喜欢的是对抗，喜欢主角之类的，有时候你知道自己是反派，有时候你是英雄，”霍纳在采访中解释道。“就我而言，我可能更多是反派，因为这符合他们制作电视节目的叙事需要。”
如果叙事剪辑如此无情，那么显而易见的问题是，为什么霍纳和红牛继续给予奈飞如此不受限制的访问权限。答案正如一级方程式赛车中一贯的情况一样，归结为赤裸裸的财务考量。
霍纳心甘情愿地承受了公众的强烈反对，因为这部纪录片系列为锦标赛注入了数十亿美元，将红牛车队从一个非常成功的赛车运动部门转变为全球占主导地位的商业巨头。
克里斯蒂安·霍纳，红牛车队领队
当被问及这部流媒体剧集的实际影响时，霍纳毫不犹豫。
“巨大。它在这项运动中绝对是颠覆性的，”霍纳指出。“反过来，车队的估值相比《极速求生》之前已经飙升到平流层。所以它产生了巨大的影响。”
这种平流层式财务增长带来的后果，是一个从根本上改变了的车迷群体。现代一级方程式时代带来了数百万新观众，他们把它当作部落战争来对待，严重两极分化了维修区墙顶层的那些人物。
尽管社交媒体上经常出现针对他的激烈攻击，霍纳对公众的看法完全不为所动。无论车迷们视他为带领车队拿下14个世界冠军的无情谋略家，还是把他看作疏远竞争对手的有毒反派，霍纳都接受扮演反派角色不过是在现代赛车运动绝对巅峰做生意的代价。
“我认为你必须明白，体育是两极分化的，”霍纳反思道。“你会有人喜欢你，也会有人不喜欢你，你只需要对自己感到自在。”
detailEn: Christian Horner reveals why Netflix made him the villain of "Drive to Survive"
Christian Horner addresses his polarising "Drive to Survive" villain edit and how Netflix transformed his F1 reputation
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

Before Netflix brought its cameras into the Formula 1 paddock, team principals were largely viewed as calculating, stoic directors operating quietly from the pitwall. By the time Christian Horner left, the role had evolved into something entirely different. He was no longer just a racing executive; he was one of the most recognisable and fiercely debated antagonists in global television.

Talking with 60 Minutes Australia, Horner addressed the massive cultural shift that completely transformed his public reputation. While some former paddock figures heavily resent their portrayal on Drive to Survive, the 52-year-old takes a highly pragmatic view of his infamous "villain" edit.
Over its multi-season run, the Netflix docuseries struck gold by showing Formula 1 not just as a motorsport, but as a high-stakes corporate soap opera.

At the centre of that drama was Horner, who was frequently pitted against Mercedes boss Toto Wolff and McLaren CEO Zak Brown. The production crews capitalised on every sarcastic press conference remark, every slammed headset, and every bitter political dispute - from the explosive 2021 Abu Dhabi title decider to Red Bull's highly publicised 2022 cost cap breach.
Christian Horner, Team Principal, Red Bull Racing
Horner is under no illusions regarding how the production team edited those interactions to create a compelling, highly dramatised narrative.

"What they love is a rivalry, and they love a protagonist or whatever, and sometimes you know you're the villain, sometimes you're the hero," Horner explained during the interview. "In my case, I was probably more the villain because it suited their rhetoric for making a TV show."

If the narrative edit was so ruthless, the obvious question is why Horner and Red Bull continued to grant Netflix such unfettered access. The answer, as is always the case in Formula 1, comes down to raw financials.

Horner willingly absorbed the public backlash because the docuseries was injecting billions of dollars into the championship, transforming Red Bull Racing from a highly successful motorsport division into a globally dominant commercial juggernaut.
Christian Horner, Team Principal, Red Bull Racing
When asked about the actual impact of the streaming series, Horner did not hesitate.

"Huge. It's been an absolute gamechanger in the sport," Horner noted. "And in turn the valuation of the teams has gone stratospheric in comparison [to] where they were pre-Drive to Survive. So it had an enormous effect."

The consequence of that stratospheric financial growth was a fundamentally changed fanbase. The modern era of Formula 1 brought in millions of new viewers who treated it like tribal warfare, heavily polarising the figures at the top of the pitwall.

Despite the intense vitriol frequently directed his way across social media, Horner remains entirely unbothered by his public perception. Whether fans view him as a ruthless mastermind who delivered 14 World Championships or a toxic antagonist who alienated rival teams, Horner accepts that playing the villain was simply the cost of doing business at the absolute pinnacle of modern motorsport.

"I think you've got to understand that sport is polarising," Horner reflected. "You're gonna have people that like you, you're gonna have people that don't, and you've just got to be comfortable in yourself."

霍纳离开时，这一角色已演变为完全不同的形态：他不再只是赛车高管，而是全球电视上最具辨识度、也最受激烈争议的反派人物之一。

items.originalTitle: Daniel Ricciardo opens door to racing return with Max Verstappen at Le Mans
items.summaryEn: Former Formula 1 driver Daniel Ricciardo has said he would consider a one-off appearance at the Le Mans 24 Hours and named his former Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen as his first choice to share a car with.
detailZh: 里卡多考虑与维斯塔潘搭档出战勒芒
里卡多透露，他会考虑在勒芒24小时耐力赛中进行一次性复出参赛
里卡多，红牛车队第三车手，与马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队
赛道之外的赛车文化。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计，以及让赛车超越运动本身的故事。
前一级方程式车手丹尼尔·里卡多透露，他会考虑在勒芒24小时耐力赛中进行一次性的亮相，并点名他的前红牛队友马克斯·维斯塔潘作为他首选的共享赛车人选。
这位澳大利亚车手自2024年新加坡大奖赛后退出F1以来便未再参赛，但在参加《F1超越格子旗》节目时，这位八次大奖赛冠军得主表示，他希望有机会按照自己的方式结束赛车生涯。
“一年前，我会说我再也不会戴上头盔了。我结束了。就这样。但内心深处有个声音告诉我，能按照自己的方式为赛车生涯画上句号，那会很好。
“所以去做这样一件事，当我摘下头盔时，我是面带微笑、快乐的，也许那就是我需要的最后一点释怀。”
丹尼尔·里卡多与马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队
里卡多表示，完整的一个赛季仍然无法吸引他，但在勒芒的一次性出战是他觉得自己可以去做的事情。对这位前红牛车手而言，吸引力的一部分在于与队友共享一辆赛车，而不是像在F1中那样作为对手相互竞争。
“与其他车手共享一辆赛车，并且真正拥有可以分享数据、互相帮助的队友，”他继续说道。“我会很享受这一点。那会是我真正喜欢的那种驾驶方式和伙伴情谊。”
当被问及他希望在耐力赛中与谁共享一辆赛车时，里卡多补充道：“我不想给他施加压力，但显然马克斯是一个会高居名单前列的名字。”
“我们显然在2018年谈过红牛以及‘如果会怎样’，而我当时正试图在职业生涯末期回到那支车队。所以也许那是一种方式，我们可以，是的，我说给大家他们想要的。”
detailEn: Daniel Ricciardo opens door to racing return with Max Verstappen at Le Mans
Daniel Ricciardo has revealed he would consider a one-off return to racing at the Le Mans 24 Hours
Daniel Ricciardo, Third Driver, Red Bull Racing and Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.

Former Formula 1 driver Daniel Ricciardo has revealed he would consider a one-off appearance at the Le Mans 24 Hours and named his former Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen as his first choice to share a car with.

The Australian driver has not raced since his F1 exit after the 2024 Singapore Grand Prix, but during an appearance on the F1 Beyond the Grid, the eight-time grand prix winner said he would like the chance to end his racing career on his own terms.

“A year ago, I would have said I will never put a helmet on again. I’m done. That’s it. But there is something there where I’m like, it’d be nice for me to also finish a racing career a bit more on my terms.
"So to do something that, when I take the helmet off, I’m smiling and happy, and maybe that’s the last bit of closure I need."
Daniel Ricciardo & Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing

Ricciardo said a full season still did not appeal to him, but that a one-off outing at Le Mans was something he could see himself doing. Part of the appeal for the former Red Bull driver is sharing a car with his team-mates, rather than competing against them as rivals in F1.

"To share a car with other drivers and to actually have real team-mates to share data and help out," he continued. "I would just enjoy it. It would be the form of driving and companionship that I would really enjoy."
Asked who he would love to share a car with in the endurance race, Ricciardo added: "I don’t want to put pressure on him, but obviously Max is a name that would be high on the list.

"We talked about Red Bull obviously in 2018 and ‘what if’, and I was trying to get back at the team at the end of my career. So maybe that’s a way that we could, yeah, I say give the people what they want."

items.originalTitle: Daniel Ricciardo reveals major regret over 2018 Red Bull departure
detailZh: 丹尼尔·里卡多透露对2018年离开红牛的重大遗憾
丹尼尔·里卡多承认他希望留在红牛而不是在2019年加入雷诺
丹尼尔·里卡多，红牛车队支持西海岸鹰队在AFL决赛中
对于红牛车迷来说，关注红牛车队，了解F1新闻、车手更新、技术洞察和米尔顿凯恩斯的比赛分析。
丹尼尔·里卡多承认他希望自己没有在2018赛季结束后离开红牛一级方程式车队。
这位澳大利亚人在红牛车队赢得了七个大奖赛，但他在离开车队并加入雷诺车队参加2019赛季时震惊了所有人，留下马克斯·维斯塔潘成为车队无可争议的主车手。这位荷兰人在2021年连续赢得了四个世界冠军，而里卡多在2021年蒙扎为麦凯伦赢得了一场比赛后，他的F1生涯在2024年结束。
在Beyond The Grid播客中，里卡多确认车队希望他留下，并承认回顾过去，他会做出不同的选择。
“如果我要简要回答，是的。我想我会希望留下，对吧？我说我想，这听起来并不令人信服。我希望留下，但，我不知道，当时我离开是因为我觉得自己有点过于舒适，有点自满。我认为有一种尝试新事物的渴望。所以我不知道，这并不是黑白分明。”
这位37岁的车手表示，这次转会让他失去了可能是他赢得世界冠军的最佳机会。
“如果我能成为世界冠军，是的，那是我最好的机会吗？是的，绝对是的。所以从这个角度来看，我想，‘是的，我真的很想了解如果我留下会是什么样子。’我不想说我还在为此困扰，但这是我感兴趣的一个未知数，我想知道那会怎样发展。”
里卡多小心翼翼地没有声称他会打败维斯塔潘，他说那样做是不公平的。但他坚持当时他仍然处于最佳状态，这由他在摩纳哥大奖赛中的胜利和那年他在墨西哥的杆位证明。
丹尼尔·里卡多，麦凯轮车队，在迈阿密开幕式舞台上拍照，站在麦凯轮赛车公司首席执行官扎克·布朗和麦凯轮车手兰多·诺里斯面前。
“我不怀疑自己保持与马克斯竞争的能力，”他说。“从那时起，很明显，是的，我的职业生涯经历了一些……河流有点风大且波涛汹涌。所以，是的，那是一个转折点。”
他补充说：“如果我能再次经历它，我会留下吗？我对会发生什么绝对好奇吗？是的，答案是肯定的。所以如果你想要称之为遗憾、好奇或者其他什么，那么我会说我有。”
里卡多后来回到了红牛车队，先是作为2023年的预备车手，然后为它的第二支车队赛车，在2024年新加坡大奖赛之后，由于在车队的不稳定时期，他被淘汰了。
detailEn: Daniel Ricciardo reveals major regret over 2018 Red Bull departure
Daniel Ricciardo has admitted he wishes he had stayed at Red Bull rather than joining Renault in 2019
Daniel Ricciardo, Red Bull Racing supports The West Coast Eagles in the AFL Final
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.
Daniel Ricciardo has admitted he wishes he had stayed at the Red Bull Formula 1 team rather than leaving at the end of the 2018 season.

The Australian won seven grands prix with Red Bull, but shocked everyone when he left the team and joined Renault for 2019, leaving Max Verstappen as the team’s undisputed lead driver. The Dutchman went on to win four consecutive world titles from 2021, while Ricciardo won just one more race - for McLaren at Monza in 2021 - before his F1 career ended in 2024.
Speaking on the Beyond The Grid podcast, the Australian confirmed the team had wanted him to stay, and admitted that, looking back, he would have done things differently.

“If I’m to answer it shortly, yes. I guess I wish I would have stayed, right? I say I guess, that doesn’t sound convincing. I wish I would have stayed but, I don’t know, also at the time I left because I felt I was getting a bit comfortable, a bit complacent. I think there was a desire to try something else. So I don’t know, it’s not that black and white.”
The 37-year-old said the move had cost him what was likely his best chance of fighting for a world championship.

“If I could have been a world champion, yes, was that my best opportunity? Yeah, absolutely. So from that point of view, I’m like, ‘Yeah, I would have loved to have known another reality of if I stayed.’ I don’t want to say it haunts me, but it’s the one unknown that I’m like, I’m so interested how that would have panned out.”

Ricciardo was careful not to claim he would have beaten Verstappen, saying it would be “unfair” to suggest that. But he did insist that he was still at the top of his game at the time, proven by his win at the Monaco Grand Prix and his pole position in Mexico that year.
Daniel Ricciardo, McLaren, takes a photo on stage at the Miami Opening Party, in front of Zak Brown, CEO, McLaren Racing, Lando Norris, McLaren

“I’m not doubting my abilities to have kept competing with Max,” he said. “It’s clear that from that point on, yes, my career took some... the river was a little windy and rough. So, yeah, that was a pivotal moment.”

He added: “If I could relive it again, would I stay? And am I absolutely curious about what would have happened? Yes, the answer is yes. So if you want to call it regret or curiosity or whatever, then I will say yes.”

Ricciardo later returned to the Red Bull family, first as a reserve driver in 2023 and then racing for its second team, before being dropped after the 2024 Singapore Grand Prix after a turbulent time at the outfit.

items.originalTitle: FIA to use AI to help shape future F1 regulations in new AWS partnership
items.summaryEn: The FIA has signed a global partnership with Amazon Web Services (AWS) and will use its artificial intelligence technology to help draw up the rules for Formula 1's next era of cars.
detailZh: 国际汽联将利用亚马逊云科技（AWS）的人工智能协助制定F1未来规则，此前已与这家科技巨头签署新的全球合作伙伴协议。
国际汽联已与亚马逊云科技合作，在制定未来F1规则时使用人工智能。
赛道之外的赛车文化。车手生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计，以及让赛车超越运动本身的故事。
国际汽车联合会（FIA）在与这家科技巨头签署新的全球合作伙伴协议后，将使用亚马逊云科技（AWS）的人工智能来帮助制定F1下一代赛车的规则。
根据该协议，AWS 成为该管理机构的官方人工智能与云计算合作伙伴，其技术将应用于包括 F1 在内的各项赛车运动。
最大的变化将体现在未来规则的制定方式上。国际汽联已经使用 AWS 的计算能力来运行其空气动力学模拟。如今，AWS 还将让国际汽联的技术与工程人员使用人工智能工具，以帮助他们起草规则。
“技术正在改变我们这项运动的每一个环节，国际汽联必须引领这一变革，”国际汽联主席穆罕默德·本·苏拉耶姆解释道。
“我们与 AWS 的新合作将支持从未来赛车到基层俱乐部的一切，许多职业生涯正是从这些基层俱乐部起步。通过将世界一流的云与人工智能技术引入国际汽联的核心，我们可以让车手、官员和志愿者更简便地参与其中，帮助我们的会员俱乐部更高效地运作，并更接近我们让全球赛车运动参与人数翻倍的雄心。我很高兴欢迎 AWS 加入国际汽联大家庭。”
安德烈亚·基米·安东内利，梅赛德斯，穆罕默德·本·苏拉耶姆，国际汽联主席
AWS 全球赛事、体育与娱乐总监克里斯汀·沙夫补充道：“赛车运动是世界上要求最高、数据最丰富的环境之一，而国际汽联正处在其中心——管理这项运动、制定规则，并为人们在各个层面参与创造机会。”
“我们很自豪成为国际汽联的官方人工智能合作伙伴，并带来 AWS 的云与人工智能能力，在赛事的各个层面支持他们的使命。”
AWS 还将成为国际汽联颁奖典礼以及国际汽联可持续创新系列的官方合作伙伴。
detailEn: FIA to use AI to help shape future F1 regulations in new AWS partnership
The FIA has partnered with Amazon Web Services to use artificial intelligence in developing future Formula 1 regulations
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.

The Fédération Internationale de l'Automobile (FIA) will use artificial intelligence from Amazon Web Services (AWS) to help draw up the rules for Formula 1's next era of cars, after signing a new global partnership with the tech giant.
Under the deal, AWS becomes the governing body's official AI and cloud computing partner, with its technology to be used across motorsport, including F1.

The biggest change will be felt in how future rules are written. The FIA already uses AWS computing power to run its aerodynamic simulations. Now, AWS will also give the FIA's technical and engineering staff access to AI tools to help them draw up regulations.
"Technology is changing every part of our sport, and the FIA must lead that change," FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem explained.

"Our new partnership with AWS will support everything from the cars of the future to the grassroots clubs where so many careers begin. By bringing world-class cloud and AI technology into the heart of the FIA, we can make it simpler for drivers, officials and volunteers to take part, help our Member Clubs work more efficiently, and move closer to our ambition of doubling global motor sport participation. I am delighted to welcome AWS to the FIA family."
Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Mohammed Ben Sulayem, FIA President

Global director of events, sports and entertainment at AWS, Kristin Shaff, added: "Motor sport is one of the most demanding and data-rich environments in the world, and the FIA sits at the center of it — governing the sport, shaping the regulations, and creating opportunities for people to participate at every level.
"We're proud to become the FIA's official AI partner and bring AWS's cloud and AI capabilities to support their mission, across every level of the sport."
AWS will also become an official partner of the FIA Awards and of the FIA Sustainable Innovation Series.
